home: My rental agreement prohibits drilling holes in the walls.
My living-room doorway is only 68 centimeters wide, so any furniture I bring in has to fit through it.
My living room has a marble floor that must not be cleaned with acidic cleaners.
My bedroom rug is made of wool and cannot be treated with chlorine bleach.
My window frames are aluminum and cannot hold magnetic curtain brackets.
The paint on my hallway walls is a matte finish that cannot be scrubbed with abrasive pads.
My dining table is solid untreated oak and must not be soaked in water.
My bathroom has no electrical socket near the mirror.
My apartment balcony has no outdoor electrical outlet.
My washing machine is a front-loading model and requires low-sudsing detergent.
My electric clothes dryer has a vent that must remain unobstructed.
My fitted bookshelves have a maximum shelf depth of 22 centimeters.
My interior door hinges are brass and must not be cleaned with ammonia-based polish.
My ceiling is a suspended tile ceiling that cannot support a hanging light fixture.
My exterior window is a sideways-sliding window, so it does not accept standard vertical-window mounts.
My wall clock runs on one AA battery and must not be connected to mains electricity.
tech: My old spare laptop has only 2 GB of RAM, so memory-heavy applications do not run on it.
My backup desktop has no Bluetooth adapter, so it cannot connect directly to Bluetooth accessories.
My document scanner connects through SCSI and has no USB interface.
My older photo printer accepts a USB-B cable and has no wireless connection.
My home router supports only 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, not 5 GHz.
My old computer monitor accepts DVI input and has no HDMI socket.
My compact camera accepts only SDHC memory cards with a maximum capacity of 32 GB.
My spare projector accepts VGA input and has no digital video input.
My e-reader supports EPUB files but does not open proprietary Kindle formats.
My film camera uses Canon FD-mount lenses, not the newer EF-mount lenses.
My old handheld game console charges through its proprietary connector rather than USB-C.
My external hard-drive enclosure takes a 2.5-inch SATA drive and cannot fit a 3.5-inch drive.
My network-attached storage has two drive bays and supports only SATA drives.
My older audio recorder accepts a 3.5 mm microphone input but has no XLR connector.
My desktop keyboard uses a PS/2 connector and cannot plug directly into a USB-only machine.
My flatbed scanner only works with a 12-volt center-positive power adapter.
hobby: My bicycle wheels use Presta valves, so a pump head made only for Schrader valves does not fit.
My sewing machine requires class 15 bobbins and cannot use class 66 bobbins.
My old typewriter takes 13-millimeter ink ribbons and cannot use cartridge ribbons.
My fountain pen uses bottled fountain-pen ink and must not be filled with India ink.
My telescope mount accepts a Vixen-style dovetail plate rather than a Losmandy plate.
My record player produces phono-level output and needs a phono preamplifier.
My analog synthesizer has five-pin MIDI sockets and no USB-MIDI interface.
My acoustic violin is full size and requires 4/4-size replacement strings.
My watercolor sketchbook contains uncoated cellulose paper that cannot tolerate repeated heavy washes.
My pottery kiln cannot exceed 1,100 degrees Celsius, so it cannot fire high-temperature porcelain.
My craft cutting mat is self-healing plastic and must not be exposed to a hot iron.
My airbrush has solvent-sensitive seals and must not be cleaned with acetone.
My embroidery hoop is 15 centimeters in diameter, so a larger design will not fit in one placement.
My precision rotary tool accepts only 2.35-millimeter round shanks, so standard 6.35-millimeter hex bits cannot fit.
My model railway track is HO scale and cannot run N-scale rolling stock.
My chessboard has 50-millimeter squares, so oversized tournament pieces do not fit comfortably.
